sources.name: The Guardian Technology
sources.title: Elon Musk joins 165,000 others calling for Nvidia to bring back Jensen Huang in open letter
sources.text: CEO ousted after affair with suspected Chinese spy reportedly plans comeback, but US treasury secretary urges ‘dramatic shake-up’ Megaspeed says it’s a ‘legitimate and lawful business’ Elon Musk and a host of other tech bosses have called for Jensen Huang’s reinstatement at Nvidia, amid reports the former chief executive is already plotting a return to the chip company just four days after his resignation. An open letter that has more than 165,000 signatories demands that the company’s board members “bring Jensen back while an independent investigation establishes the facts”. Huang’s resignation on Thursday ended a 33-year run at the helm of the AI company he co-founded, after reports he had at least two extramarital affairs, one with a woman accused of spying for China and another with a subordinate. According to the Financial Times , Huang has discussed a possible return to the company with people close to him. One Huang ally told the paper they were putting together ⁠a “war room” of Silicon Valley executives to lobby ​for the former Nvidia ‌CEO’s return ‌and would try to garner support from ‌the White House. “Everyone that matters in tech outside the frontier labs loves Jensen,” the person said, adding that the efforts had Huang’s support. On Friday, two big shareholders, the investors Brad Gerstner and Gavin Baker, urged the board to keep “all options” open. In Washington, however, the US treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, argued on Sunday that Nvidia should look outside the company for its next CEO. “They need a dramatic shake-up,” Bessent said on Fox News. Bessent also called on Nvidia to explain whether it had knowingly allowed its most advanced AI chips to reach China, saying this was more important than Huang’s affair with the alleged spy for Beijing, Alice Huang. The US forbids sales to China of the most cutting-edge AI chips as parts of its strategy to stay ahead of Beijing in the race to dominate artificial intelligence. In late 2025, Trump authorised sales of Nvidia chips called H200s to China, but not the most advanced chips used to run AI models reshaping modern society. “Nothing above the H200s can be sold to the Chinese,” Bessent said, adding that it was important to examine “whether Nvidia had a culture of compliance around the US export restrictions”. Bessent said he wanted answers from Nvidia and its internal investigation of Jensen Huang’s behaviour within the next 10 days. One analyst downplayed the prospect of a Huang return, describing the notion of the ex-CEO’s reinstatement as “ridiculous”. Dan Ives, an analyst at Yorkville Ives, said the range of issues facing Huang and Nvidia, from personal conduct to questions over China, made an external candidate or the permanent appointment of the interim CEO – Nvidia’s chief financial officer, Colette Kress – the best option. “We see no chance Jensen comes back to Nvidia as CEO and for the company the best path forward is with a new external CEO or Colette,” he said, describing the petition as “noise and distraction”. US lawmakers have said Donald Trump’s administration must answer questions on what it knew about Huang’s relationship with the suspected Chinese spy. Jensen Huang has agreed to appear before the House select committee on China, as well as the foreign affairs and the intelligence committees. The dates of the appearances, likely to be behind closed doors, have not been confirmed. On Sunday, Megaspeed, the Singapore-based company where Alice Haung was an executive until she left in 2025, said it was a “ legitimate and lawful business ”. In the past three years, the company was one of Nvidia’s biggest foreign customers, buying nearly $5bn (£3.8bn) in AI chips and advanced hardware. Alongside Musk, the tech heavyweight signatories on the letter calling for Jensen Huang’s return include Tim Sweeney, the founder and CEO of the video game publisher Epic Games, and Garry Tan, the president of Y Combinator, San Francisco’s most renowned business incubator. Another signatory, the Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick, wrote that Huang had “erred, yes – to err is to be human – but I do not believe anything he has done rises to the bar of separating him from his company”. More than 7,500 signatories identified themselves as Nvidia employees, equivalent to 18% of the company’s workforce. The support illustrates the unique standing of Huang, who is seen within the industry as a godfather of AI . Under his leadership, Nvidia became a pivotal Silicon Valley investor, financing datacentres and startups, earning it the nickname “the central bank of AI”. But the company – which will report on its quarterly earnings on Tuesday – has also faced criticism that it has fuelled a speculative investment bubble. Huang fought any constraints on the AI race, clashing on these issues with the Claude creator, Anthropic, and its chief executive, Dario Amodei. Agence France-Presse and Reuters contributed to this report

sources.title: Nvidia board is not considering bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO, source tells CNBC
sources.text: Nvidia's board of directors is not considering bringing back Jensen Huang as CEO, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC. The board is focused on an investigation into Huang, and is not in discussions to bring him back, said the person, who spoke on condition of anonymity in order to discuss internal matters. Nvidia has hired law firm Wachtell Lipton to lead a probe into Huang's conduct and whether it compromised national security or company secrets. Last week, Huang resigned from Nvidia, the company he founded, after 33 years as CEO. The resignation came days after Huang admitted to an affair, and news stories alleged he had an affair with Alice Huang, who worked for a customer and is alleged to have contact with Chinese intelligence, as well as affairs with employees at Nvidia. Over the weekend, the Financial Times reported that Huang had discussed coming back with allies. Altimeter Capital's Brad Gerstner told CNBC on Monday that Huang had not discussed a comeback with him. A representative for Huang declined to comment on speculation on Sunday. Many in the tech world have called for Huang to return as Nvidia CEO. An online petition calling for his reinstatement has drawn 180,000 signatures as well as support from major figures including Elon Musk , Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney. President Donald Trump said on Monday that he is open to Jensen Huang returning as CEO of Nvidia. "It was not put at risk, and our country is now stronger than ever before," Trump told reporters when asked about U.S. national security concerns. On Friday, a representative for Nvidia's board said it was in the process of selecting a search firm for the Nvidia CEO role.

sources.title: The open-source movement wants Jensen Huang back
sources.text: Supporters are signing a petition to reinstate Huang. But findings on Nvidia chips in China and a new Commerce rule are threatening open-source AI’s reputation and progress regardless. This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here . On Friday, a petition to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia began circulating on social media, and by Monday it listed some notable signatories, including Elon Musk and several influential Nvidia researchers. But comb through the more than 115,000 names and you’ll notice a significant faction of Huang’s supporters—higher-ups from Hugging Face, a hub for sharing AI models, and venture capital firms Andreessen Horowitz and Sequoia Capital—come from a particular slice of the tech world. These names have a vested interest in the development of open-source AI, models that, unlike ChatGPT or Claude, can be downloaded and run independent of large tech companies. Supporters of such models say that concentrating AI in the hands of a few powerful companies will leave everyone else worse off (a concern that wouldn’t sound out of place among the AI industry's critics on the left, if so many open-source advocates weren’t also venture capitalists who stand to profit when startups can build on cheaper AI without paying Big Tech). Huang had become a sort of ringleader for those who defend open source to policymakers against concerns that such models come with no guardrails and cede AI leadership to China, where the most powerful and popular open-source models are created. They now want their most influential voice returned to his post. But it’s not just Huang’s extramarital affairs that threaten his (and Nvidia’s) credibility as an advocate for open-source AI. New research into China’s startups using Nvidia’s chips, and a new rule from the US Department of Commerce announced Monday, could deal a blow to both the movement’s reputation and its technical progress. On Thursday, the day Huang resigned, ex-OpenAI researcher Will DePue published findings online suggesting that China’s AI companies had far more access to Nvidia’s advanced Blackwell chips than previously estimated. China is banned from accessing Nvidia’s most cutting-edge chips to help protect America’s AI lead. It’s unclear how they would have gained access to the chips. DePue claims the results were verified by senior researchers at OpenAI and Anthropic, but an independent analysis has not confirmed the results. (DePue did not respond to a request for an interview. Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment.) The findings do not establish that Nvidia helped Chinese companies obtain the chips, and the broader problem of chip smuggling was already known to extend well beyond Nvidia’s control. But in suggesting that Nvidia may have profited from the rise of Chinese AI startups, whose models are increasingly being used by American companies instead of domestic alternatives, the findings do leave Huang in an awkward position. He has championed open-source AI as a way to strengthen American technological leadership. “Without open source, startups can’t thrive, university researchers can’t do research, you can’t teach AI, scientists can’t use AI,” he said last December during a talk about helping the US win the AI race against China. It also makes the idea of reinstating Huang even more of a long shot. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent even said last week that Nvidia should not consider someone from inside the company to replace him. The new findings lower Huang’s chances further. What happens next? Nvidia announced in September it would acquire Hugging Face for nearly $13 billion. Its support for open source also serves a straightforward financial interest: The more businesses that build their own models instead of forking over money to Anthropic and OpenAI, the more chips Nvidia can sell. But a new rule from the US Department of Commerce could mean the models popular on Hugging Face will soon stop getting smarter. The rule aims to prevent Chinese companies from training models on Nvidia chips that they can’t own directly, but that they can access remotely in data centers in countries like Malaysia—a workaround that has helped China’s open-source models get so good. The open-source world rallied around Huang because of his influence on policymakers. That was important, since the rise of China’s open-source models has splintered some in Trump’s orbit. If Huang is out, who is next? Ten years after AlphaGo’s match against Go champion Lee Sedol, today’s AI still isn’t tapping into the machinery that made that win possible. An exclusive interview with Nick Cammarata, the researcher whose 26,000-word viral blog post has AI safety folks celebrating. sources.title: Nvidia’s board is reportedly ‘not considering’ hiring Jensen Huang back
sources.text: Nvidia’s board of directors is still focused on an investigation into Huang, CNBC reports. Nvidia’s board of directors is still focused on an investigation into Huang, CNBC reports. Nvidia’s board of directors “isn’t considering” having Jensen Huang return as CEO, according to a report from CNBC . A source tells the outlet the board “is focused on an investigation into Huang, and is not in discussions to bring him back.” Since Huang’s resignation last week , tech executives, along with current and former Nvidia employees, have called for his reinstatement. An online petition to bring Huang back as CEO has amassed more than 180,000 signatures , including from major figures like Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, and Replit CEO Amjad Masad. President Donald Trump said on Monday that it “certainly isn’t a bad idea” for Huang to return to Nvidia. A report from the Financial Times also suggests that Huang floated the idea of returning as CEO with some of his colleagues. Nvidia appointed its chief financial officer, Colette Kress, as interim CEO. The company has also hired Wachtell Lipton to investigate Huang’s conduct .

sources.title: Jensen Huang discute un posible retorno a la dirección de Nvidia, según 'FT'
sources.text: Jensen Huang , cofundador de Nvidia , estaría discutiendo con posibles aliados un potencial regreso a la dirección de la compañía que ayudó a crear en 1993 y de la que era consejero delegado hasta su renuncia el pasado jueves tras salir a la luz varias infidelidades , incluida una relación con una presunta espía china, además de con una subordinada. Según informa Financial Times , que cita fuentes conocedoras, el carismático líder tecnológico estaría considerando la posibilidad de regresar como CEO de Nvidia , mientras aliados en Silicon Valley presionan a la junta directiva de la compañía, que está realizando una investigación interna sobre la conducta del ejecutivo, para que lo reincorpore días después de que se viera forzado a renunciar al cargo. En este sentido, un aliado de Huang declaró al periódico que estaban organizando un grupo de trabajo con ejecutivos de Silicon Valley para presionar de cara al regreso del exconsejero delegado de Nvidia para lo que intentarían obtener el apoyo de la Casa Blanca . "Todos los que importan en el sector tecnológico fuera de los laboratorios de vanguardia admiran a Jensen ", afirmó, añadiendo que el propio Huang apoyaba estos esfuerzos. Una campaña pública para restituir al CEO de Nvidia ha cobrado fuerza durante el fin de semana al sumar a personalidades como Elon Musk , CEO de Tesla y SpaceX, y Tim Sweeney , consejero delegado de Epic Games , a los ejecutivos que respaldaron una carta pública reclamando que la junta directiva "Traiga de vuelta a Jensen". Brad Gerstner , fundador de Altimeter Capital , y Gavin Baker , director de Atreides Management , ambos accionistas de Nvidia, publicaron el viernes una carta abierta en la que pedían al consejo de administración de la compañía considerar "todas las opciones, incluido el posible regreso de Jensen Huang". Asimismo, el diario destaca que Huang sigue gozando de una lealtad inquebrantable entre algunos empleados , varios de los cuales han manifestado públicamente su petición de regreso tras su renuncia. No obstante, advierte que cualquier intento de restituirle al frente de Nvidia probablemente se enfrente a la oposición de importantes legisladores en Washington , mientras que el secretario del Tesoro de EEUU , Scott Bessent, pidió este domingo una " reorganización drástica " en el liderazgo de la empresa tras la salida de Huang. A este respecto, el periódico apunta que, incluso los aliados de Huang dudaban sobre cómo rehabilitar la reputación del ex CEO de la empresa, ya que "tener una relación extramatrimonial con una subordinada es motivo de despido ", según reconoció una persona involucrada en los esfuerzos por la readmisión de Huang. El pasado jueves, junto con la renuncia de Jensen Huang como consejero delegado, Nvidia anunció la designación como máxima ejecutiva interina de Colette Kress , actual vicepresidenta ejecutiva y directora financiera de la empresa, hasta que se complete el proceso de sucesión , para lo que el consejo de administración comenzó la búsqueda de un sustituto, teniendo en cuenta candidatos tanto internos como externos. A este respecto, Financial Times informó de que la junta de Nvidia se ha puesto en contacto con René Haas , consejero delegado de Arm , como posible sucesor de Huang. sources.text: A divisão gamer da Nvidia pode acabar? Saiba o futuro da linha GeForce após saída de Jensen Huang A renúncia de Jensen Huang ao cargo de CEO da Nvidia, oficializada na última quinta-feira (12) , está longe de virar um assunto encerrado na indústria. Até mesmo o próprio executivo, segundo o Financial Times , agora está reconsiderando tentar voltar ao cargo. De acordo com a reportagem, Huang teria discutido com pessoas próximas a possibilidade de retornar à cadeira de gerente executivo. Uma das fontes citou até a montagem de uma “sala de guerra” formada por executivos do Vale do Silício para iniciar um lobby a favor da restituição. Um dos objetivos do grupo é conseguir o apoio da Casa Branca , que é uma peça bastante interessada no futuro da Nvidia. Por ser um dos pilares do setor de inteligência artificial (IA) e uma das empresa mais valiosas do mundo, ela tem papel relevante em negociações com marcas locais e estrangeiras. “Todo mundo que importa no mundo da tecnologia fora dos laboratórios de modelos de fronteira ama o Jensen”, teria dito uma pessoa próxima ao assunto. Até o momento, tanto a Nvidia quanto o próprio Huang não se manifestaram sobre a reportagem. Huang renunciou na última semana após a revelação de que ele manteve dois casos extraconjugais: um relacionamento com uma executiva que pode ser uma espiã chinesa , uma diretora de divisão da Nvidia e possivelmente outra funcionária ainda identificada também da empresa de chips. Funcionários da companhia estão se manifestando em chats internos pedindo uma possível volta do executivo ao cargo para o conselho de diretores da marca, que ainda está investigando o caso. Além disso, um abaixo-assinado que pede ao conselho o retorno de Huang ao menos enquanto o relatório não for divulgado já tem mais de 175 mil assinaturas. Além de fãs e funcionários, ela tem apoio inclusive de figuras como Elon Musk , Tim Sweeney (CEO da Epic Games) e Garry Tan, CEO da incubadora de startups Y Combinator. Quem exatamente é Dario Amodei, CEO da Anthropic e prestes a realizar o maior IPO da história? Entenda nesta matéria ! /Com informações de Financial Times. sources.title: Reviravolta: Jensen Huang articula retorno à NVIDIA com apoio de Elon Musk e Tim Sweeney
sources.text: Por André Lourenti Magalhães • Editado por Jones Oliveira | 16/11/2026 às 14:02 Jensen Huang renunciou ao cargo de CEO da NVIDIA na última semana, mas não descarta voltar ao comando da empresa. De acordo com o site Financial Times, Huang conta com aliados no Vale do Silício para pressionar o conselho da Big Tech sobre um possível retorno . Uma das fontes ouvidas pela reportagem original afirma que há uma “sala de guerra” montada por parceiros e lobistas para trazê-lo de volta ao cargo. Há até a possibilidade de buscar apoio na Casa Branca, ainda que o caminho seja improvável — o Secretário do Tesouro dos EUA, Scott Bessent, já defendeu publicamente uma reestruturação na empresa de chips. Um dos argumentos dos aliados é de que Jensen Huang é uma pessoa querida no mercado de tecnologia. Outras fontes afirmam que o ex-CEO era o responsável por conduzir negociações importantes no mercado de IA. Um eventual retorno é apoiado até por funcionários da própria NVIDIA : comentários em caixa de sugestões internas da companhia defendem a volta do executivo. Por enquanto, a companhia é liderada de forma interina por Colette Kress, que atuava como vice-presidente executiva e diretora financeira antes da mudança. Jensen Huang também é defendido por nomes importantes do mercado, como Elon Musk e o CEO da Epic Games, Tim Sweeney . Ambos assinaram uma carta aberta pedindo para o conselho “trazer Jensen de volta” . A NVIDIA ainda não tem novas atualizações sobre o comando da empresa, mas rumores apontam que o CEO da Arm, Rene Haas, seria um dos favoritos a assumir a cadeira deixada por Huang. Jensen Huang renunciou ao cargo após confirmar um caso extraconjugal com a ex-diretora da Megaspeed International e empresária Alice Huang, acusada de espionagem a favor da China. sources.title: Nvidia stock falls as investors price in fallout from Jensen Huang's resignation
sources.text: Nvidia 's stock continued to slide in the wake of CEO Jensen Huang 's resignation , falling around 4% on Monday after the chip giant lost hundreds of billions in market cap last week. Huang resigned from Nvidia, the company's board announced on Thursday, after mounting scrutiny following reports that he had a relationship with a woman believed to be a Chinese spy. Huang told employees he had an affair in an email on Nov. 8. It was later reported that Huang had romantic relationships with two Nvidia employees. Nvidia did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment on Friday. An online petition calling for Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO has drawn more than 170,000 signatures , as prominent tech executives, including Elon Musk , rallied behind him. Meanwhile, U.S. lawmakers are pushing to launch comprehensive investigations into the scandal. Huang cofounded Nvidia in 1993 and led the company through its meteoric rise to becoming the world's most valuable company, with its AI chips underpinning the technology's boom. Nvidia appointed longtime finance chief Colette Kress as interim CEO and said its board would consider both internal and external candidates in its search for a permanent successor. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday called for a "dramatic shakeup" at Nvidia, adding that the board should look outside the company for its next chief executive. He also suggested other Nvidia executives should face scrutiny over the chip giant's compliance with U.S. export controls. — CNBC's Caleigh Keating contributed to this report.

sources.title: Nvidia Was Already in Trouble Before the Jensen Huang Mess
sources.text: Nvidia played a key role enabling the AI gold rush thanks in large part to its recently ousted CEO Jensen Huang . Huang was a master of foreseeing technological changes , investing in chips to train AI earlier than most. But just as he’s leaving , the company has a growing list of competitors with a range of new, advanced technology breathing down its neck. For Nvidia , where CFO Colette Kress has now taken the reins, the timing isn’t great. “Everything sold today was designed two-to-three years ago,” says the CEO of a large AI company, who spoke to WIRED on condition of anonymity to avoid hurting business relationships. Kress, or whoever replaces her permanently, will have to chart the course that the chip industry will take two years from now, the CEO says. Already, competitors have started to move in. Nvidia dominates the market for AI accelerators, capturing 80 percent of sales, according to Silicon Analysis. Longtime nemesis AMD is now making a concerted effort to build competitive AI chips. Its share of the market has crept up from just two percent in 2022 to between 7 and 10 percent in 2026. Big US cloud players—Google, Amazon, and Microsoft—are all developing more specialized chips to power the training and serving of AI models. Each has seen similar gains. These companies are designing their own silicon to reduce costs and to gain some independence from Nvidia. Several startups now offer more specialized chips that promise improvements over Nvidia’s core products. Cerebras, for instance, sells giant ones meant to power giant AI models. AMD recently bought Taalas, a company that burns models’ weights into silicon to make computations ultra efficient. Using these chips requires rewriting a lot of code, however, to make them work with cutting-edge AI models. Patrick Moorhead, chief analyst at MoorInStrat, a company that tracks the chip industry, says the rise of AI agents makes inference, or running models that have already been trained, more important. That’s an area where Nvidia has less of an edge compared to cloud hyperscalers and startups. Nvidia did, however, acquire a startup making specialized chips, called Groq, in December of 2025. And because of the rise in AI assistants and agents, there’s also growing demand for general purpose central processing units (CPUs), Moorhead said, an area where Nvidia barely competes. Nvidia still maintains a huge lead in AI thanks to Huang’s foresight. Huang cofounded the company in 1993 to design graphics chips for PCs. In the mid-2010s, he saw the promise of AI. He funded academic research on the topic, developed software to support AI engineering, and gave hardware to labs and startups. In 2022, ChatGPT took AI mainstream and sales of Nvidia chips skyrocketed. The company’s revenue went from $26.91 billion in January 2022 to $215.94 billion in January 2026. The challenges it faces may not be existential—but they do add up, especially on a global scale. While Nvidia’s fortunes have risen in the US, they have declined in the world’s other big market for AI, China. Washington is trying to restrict access to its most advanced chips, while Beijing is trying to develop its own chip industry. Nvidia is not allowed to sell its most powerful chips in China, but it can sell previous generations. Sales of these chips as well as non AI chips doubled over the past year, but China now accounts for only eight percent of the company’s overall revenue, compared with 20 percent in 2024, according to its fillings. It remains unclear how many chips exported to other countries may either end up in China or end up being used remotely by Chinese firms. Huawei, a Chinese tech giant targeted with US sanctions for several years, has developed new kinds of supercomputers that harness many more chips than usual to train and run AI models. Some Chinese AI companies, such as Z.ai, which makes one of the world’s best open source models, say they’ve trained their models entirely using Huawei’s chips. If Chinese open-weight models gain traction in other countries, it could create a market for Chinese chips elsewhere. Huang’s dealings with China played a major role in his downfall. He had a romantic relationship with Huang Le, also known as Alice Huang, a Chinese executive at a Singaporean company called Megaspeed who the US government suspects of being an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. Megaspeed and its subsidiaries have reportedly imported between $4.6 and $7.5 billion Nvidia chips into southeast Asia. Reports suggest that the company may have provided access to the chips to Chinese AI firms. Babak Minovi, a senior analyst at the Eurasia Group, a consultancy that focuses on technology and geopolitics, says Huang was right to point out that cutting off access to China would empower domestic rivals. “Huang was taking a pragmatic line, and he knows competition,” he says. Even in markets that it dominates, Nvidia may turn out to be a victim of its own success. The AI models built using Nvidia’s chip are automating the very elements of coding, data analysis, and scientific research that help design chips. Most chip design firms use specialized AI models to arrange components on processors—something that traditionally required deep engineering expertise and experience. And both OpenAI and Anthropic have recently touted the ability of their newest models to design electronics from scratch. Moorhead says the shift towards AI chip design may not pose a huge threat to Nvidia because it’s riding the same wave. “They have access to AI too,” he notes. But Moorhead says the way AI models can now quickly rewrite code to run on different hardware may prove a problem. For years, Nvidia has attracted developers by providing software that makes it easy to write programs and build models for its silicon.
